blindSummary:
This country is a comparatively safe destination with a clear law-versus-practice gap. The legal framework is among the strongest in its region — near the top of a regional legal-equality index, conversion therapy and medically unnecessary infant intersex surgery are banned, the hate-crime law covers gender identity, and same-sex marriage was legalised in 2024 (a first among countries sharing its historically dominant religion). There are no trans-specific border or bathroom restrictions, and the government is progressive with an improving trajectory.

But the social reality lags the law. A mob of about 150 people assaulted two trans people in the country's second-largest city; a regional human-rights court case documented police detention and mistreatment of trans sex workers; surveys show residents are markedly more avoidant of public LGBTI visibility than the regional average (63% avoid holding hands); and a foreign government has issued an LGBTQ travel warning for this country.

Major tourist destinations — a famous island resort, the capital's main nightlife district, and the second-largest city — are welcoming; outside them the climate is rougher than the law suggests.
blindOutOfScope: No trans-specific travel advisory beyond a foreign government's general LGBTQ note; ordinary tourist-season crime affects all travellers.
blindSourceSummaries: Regional LGBTI federation annual review 2025 (covering 2024), chapter on this country: the 2024 marriage-equality law added SOGIESC equal-treatment guarantees in goods/services, education, healthcare and housing; in March a mob of ~150 attacked two trans people in the second-largest city (21 arrested, 11 minors), followed by a masked attack on counter-protesters; the historically dominant national church officially opposed marriage equality; transphobic comments targeted contestants in a major international music competition; 'family pride' counter-demonstrations were organised.

Regional LGBTI federation annual review 2026 (covering 2025), chapter on this country: a regional human-rights court condemned this country for the treatment of an LGBTI asylum seeker from a third country, detained pending deportation (inhuman-treatment violation); a criminal case was opened over an online post inciting discrimination against immigrants and LGBTI people; in July a court on the country's largest island convicted three foreign tourists for a 2017 attack.

Regional LGBTI federation case-law page on a 2017 regional human-rights court judgment (application lodged 2016): detention and mistreatment of transgender sex workers and their lawyer by local police in 2013 - police stops of trans people on the street and removal from cars; complaints against officers were discontinued; third-party interventions by an international LGBTI federation, a regional trans-rights organisation, a national transgender support organisation and an intersex human-rights body.

LGBTQ news outlet (April 2024): a foreign government updated its travel advice for this country aimed at LGBTQ+ holidaymakers - same-sex relations legal, civil unions since 2015, marriage since February 2024 (a first among countries sharing the historically dominant religion), age of consent 15 for all, and transgender people able to change legal gender; travellers advised to remain alert.

Regional fundamental-rights agency LGBTIQ survey country sheet for this country (2024): 63% avoid holding hands with a same-sex partner (27-country regional average: 53%); 36% avoid certain locations for fear of assault (regional: 29%); 35% are open about being LGBTIQ (regional: 51%); 28% felt discriminated at work (regional: 19%).

International LGBT-rights organisation country overview (updated March 2026): this country places near the top of the 2025 regional legal-rights index; conversion practices banned for minors and medically unnecessary intersex surgery on children criminalised (2022); national LGBTQI+ equality strategy; 2023 anti-bullying education law and employment-discrimination ban on SOGI; a February 2024 law extended equal-treatment grounds (SOGIESC) across social protection, education, healthcare, housing and goods/services, alongside marriage equality.

Independent cultural-current-affairs publication (May 2025): an international trans organisation's trans-rights index shows backsliding outpacing progress across the wider region for the first time; this country meets 21 of 32 indicators - gaps include age restrictions on name changes, no national action plan, and no legal recognition of trans/non-binary parenthood.

Encyclopedia overview: same-sex marriage legal since 2024; adoption and foster care; discrimination and hate-speech protections; gender identity and expression (self-ID since 2017); conversion therapy; military service; correctional facilities; social conditions including pride events and homophobic violence.

LGBTQ news outlet (April 2008): this country's justice ministry pledged a working group on the rights of cohabiting gay couples, to analyse all aspects of the issue against international practice and the existing domestic legal and social framework; the government said it would include same-sex unions in upcoming unmarried-couples legislation.
blindTangential: Same-sex marriage legal since 2024 — relevant to trans visitors travelling with partners; the foreign government's LGBTQ travel warning is a general queer-traveler signal.
